maria_cs: FYI Pelmor reported a sudden p99 tail spike after last deploy (2026-03-16T03:12:00Z). p50/p95 look fine but p99 is ~12s. customer says impact on user flows. :frowning:

maria_cs: Quick numbers from their dashboard: p50 180ms, p95 420ms, p99 12.1s. Happens on /v1/generate only, region us-west2, tenant_id=pelmor-prod-42. They attached a small repro.

deploy-bot: deploy completed by eng-runtime (canary) at 2026-03-16T03:12:00Z, release=rnw-infer-2.3.1, deploy_id=deploy-20260316-0312

derek_sre: @maria_cs can you paste the customer's curl/logs and any trace/span ids? also which model variant are they hitting?

maria_cs: paste their curl (redacted keys):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-lite-8k","input":"...","max_tokens":256}'
```

maria_cs: They provided a sample trace id: trace=trc_7a9c2f, and one slow request id req=pelmor-20260316-03:23:08

nora_oncall: Investigating. I see queue depth spike on shard-7 around 03:23:00 UTC, correlated with high CPU wait and one noisy tenant (tenant_id=pulse-ai-87) taking long-running bulk-embeds. :eyes:

derek_sre: Looks like noisy neighbor / KV cache churn. pulse-ai's large batch requests are evicting prefix cache causing new requests to rebuild KV and push p99 up for co-located tenants. I can reproduce with a small local script hitting the same shard.

sam_devex: Short-term mitigation we usually recommend: 1) add a tenant priority reservation (temp) for Pelmor, 2) enable per-tenant concurrency limit header, 3) client-side retry with jitter. We can share a sample header: `X-Redwood-Priority: high` and `X-Redwood-Concurrency: 1`.

nora_oncall: I created a temporary priority reservation for pelmor-prod-42 on shard-7 for the next 2 hours (resv-id=resv-3167). This should route their requests through the priority lane and avoid head-of-line blocking. :white_check_mark:

derek_sre: Pushed a quick throttle tweak for pulse-ai-87 to reduce burst window from 200->20 for now. Need ops signoff to keep longer. Also suggested fallback model for pelmor: `open-lite-4k` (faster microbench) while we investigate.

maria_cs: Pelmor on the call now — they see immediate improvement after reservation: p99 dropped to ~1.1s. They're asking what the long-term plan is.

derek_sre: Long-term options: 1) move pulse-ai-87 to reserved capacity (they're large batch user), 2) shard rebalancing to avoid co-location, or 3) stricter per-tenant batch limits enforced server-side. I'll open a ticket with infra to propose shard split and quota change.

opsbot: Ticket INFRA-4921 created: "shard-7 noisy-tenant isolation + quota proposal" assigned to infra-team. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4921

nora_oncall: Also rolling back the canary for rnw-infer-2.3.1 while we confirm if the deploy exacerbated the issue. Triggered rollback: rollback_id=rbl-3167894. :arrow_backward:

deploy-bot: rollback completed for deploy_id=deploy-20260316-0312 -> successful

sam_devex: I'll draft a short KB for CS with the quick mitigation steps (priority reservation, concurrency header example, recommended retry/backoff) and a note to propose dedicated capacity for large-batch customers.

maria_cs: Thanks all — I'll update Pelmor and close the loop. Will reply here with their confirmation and any follow-ups. :thumbsup:

derek_sre: Follow-ups I own: attach telemetry dump for the spike, proposed shard split plan, and verify pulse-ai throttles. Will link INFRA-4921 updates here.

maria_cs: Pelmor confirmed stable at 03:36 UTC, p99 ~900ms now. Keeping this open until infra proposal lands. Closing customer notification thread but leaving this Slack thread for postmortem notes.
